title: Scientific Editor- Joule ( Energy Research)
jobDescription:
Scientific Editor- Joule ( Energy Research) Do you have a passion for sustainable energy research? Are you a PHD holder? About our Team Since its launch in 2017, Joule has quickly become established as one of the world's leading forums for cutting edge energy research and insightful analysis and commentary. Joule values having a diverse editorial team, and applications from candidates from minority groups currently under-represented in science are warmly welcomed. About the Role We are seeking a Scientific Editor based in India to join the Joule editorial team and contribute to the journal’s continued development as a leading destination for transformative energy research. Working closely with and reporting to the Editor-in-Chief, the Scientific Editor will assess and manage research submissions across Joule’s broad scope, identify emerging areas of scientific importance, commission influential content, and build strong relationships with researchers around the world. The successful candidate will help shape the scientific direction of the journal and ensure that the work published in Joule is rigorous, distinctive, impactful, and relevant to the global energy research community. Responsibilities Handling manuscripts through the editorial and peer-review process, rigorously evaluating submissions against Joule's demanding standards for scientific quality, technical rigor, originality, and broader significance, and making well-reasoned editorial decisions. Attracting submissions of high-quality research articles and commissioning reviews, perspectives, commentaries, and other editorial content from leading researchers and experts. Traveling to international conferences, workshops, and research institutions to engage with scientists, identify emerging research directions, and promote the journal and portfolio. Collaborating with editorial teams across Cell Press to understand the vision and scope of relevant journals, identify manuscripts suitable for transfer to the most appropriate journal, and strengthen the representation of energy research across the portfolio. Contributing to broader editorial and strategic projects across Cell Press. Requirements A Ph D in a field relevant to Joule's scope, preferably in chemical engineering or a closely related discipline. Candidates with expertise in catalysis, batteries, and photovoltaics are especially encouraged to apply. Prior editorial experience is preferred; exceptional early-career candidates with a strong research background will also be considered. Demonstrated ability to think conceptually and critically across a broad range of scientific and technical topics. Strong existing networks within the global energy research community, with the ability to engage effectively with researchers at all career stages and across international boundaries. Excellent written and oral communication skills in English, with the ability to communicate complex scientific ideas and editorial decisions clearly and constructively. jobDescription:
Finance SOX Manager Do you have strong experience in SOX compliance, internal controls, and audit within finance processes? Are you ready to lead control testing, stakeholder engagement, and compliance excellence within Elsevier’s Finance team? About our Team At Elsevier, our team is dedicated to developing professionals with a strong foundation in finance control, auditing, and reporting disciplines. We tackle a variety of routine compliance challenges, empowering our members to apply their knowledge in practical settings while enhancing their problem-solving skills. We foster an environment of continuous learning through mentorship, training resources, and collaborative experiences, ensuring our team stays current with industry practices and regulatory requirements. Together, we strive to create an inclusive workplace where innovative ideas are valued, and every member contributes to driving compliance and excellence within our organization. About the Role The SOX Manager is responsible for ensuring the effectiveness of internal controls in line with corporate objectives and regulatory requirements, including SOX and related standards. This role reviews, develops, implements, and maintains controls across processes, systems, financial statements, journals, and reports; identifies control gaps and drives timely remediation; ensures process documentation is regularly updated; and supports internal and external audit requirements, including management attestation activities. The role also manages a small team, sets priorities to address operational needs, and oversees team performance through objective setting, reviews, and pay recommendations, with decisions guided by policies, resources, and business plans. Responsibilities · Lead the annual SOX testing lifecycle, including planning, coordination, execution, reporting, and close-out of management testing for key financial controls. · Own and maintain the internal controls framework, including RACMs, narratives, and flowcharts, ensuring accurate documentation across significant finance processes. · Ensure comprehensive control coverage across P2P, O2C, R2R, and other relevant finance processes in line with SOX, ICFR, and financial statement assertions. · Conduct walkthroughs for in-scope financial processes to identify key controls, assess risks, and validate assertion coverage such as completeness, accuracy, and existence. · Evaluate the design and operating effectiveness of manual and automated controls to ensure they prevent or detect material misstatements. · Lead deficiency assessment, remediation planning, tracking, and re-testing to ensure timely resolution and effective control performance. · Act as the primary liaison with business stakeholders, management, external auditors, and internal audit teams to support smooth audit coordination and compliance alignment. · Manage SOX testing delivery and a small team, balancing individual responsibilities with oversight, review, stakeholder training, process improvement, transformation readiness, and ITGC collaboration. Requirements · Hold a bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related field, or possess a professional accounting and/or auditing qualification. · Bring over 8 years of relevant experience in financial reporting, SOX compliance, internal controls over financial reporting, audit, compliance, or a similar field. · Demonstrate 2–3 years of leadership experience, including managing a small team of 2–4 people and engaging effectively with stakeholders. · Have strong working knowledge of key systems and tools, including advanced Excel, Power Point, Hyperion, Oracle, and an understanding of IT general controls. · Communicate effectively in spoken and written English with a high level of clarity and professionalism. · Work effectively within multi-location and global teams across different time zones. · Apply advanced stakeholder management and engagement skills to support collaboration, alignment, and effective delivery. · Demonstrate strong integrity and the ability to speak up, escalate potential control issues promptly, and quickly learn and apply enterprise AI tools to support technical workflows and business objectives. title: Solution Architect
jobDescription:
Architect – Life Sciences Would you like to take ownership of the technology strategy for the future of Life Sciences research? Do you enjoy working alongside cross-functional technical teams to shape best-practice, AI-enabled solutions at scale? About our Team:- Our Technology teams use cutting-edge technologies to build the products and platforms that advance science and health. Within Corporate Markets, the Chemistry Solutions team is responsible for Reaxys, our flagship chemistry research and data platform, alongside the data pipelines, knowledge graphs and AI services that power it. We give researchers powerful digital tools to tackle some of the biggest problems facing the world today. About the

ROLE:
-
As Architect for the Life sciences Domain, you will own the definition, development and evolution of our Chemistry Solutions technical roadmap, centred on Reaxys. You will work closely with our Lead Architect — who sets the cross-domain architectural direction — to ensure the Chemistry Domain aligns with enterprise standards while meeting the specific needs of chemistry research, data and AI. You will partner with customers, product, engineering and business stakeholders to guide and communicate critical architectural principles, and you will stay at the forefront of emerging technology — from generative AI and large language models to knowledge graphs and cloud-native data platforms — to identify and shape the next generation of chemistry solutions.

RESPONSIBILITIES:
- Own the Chemistry Domain architecture: define, document and evolve the technology strategy and roadmap for Reaxys and our wider Chemistry Solutions, aligned to business goals and to enterprise standards working closely with the Lead Architect for Corporate Markets. Partner closely with the Lead Architect and fellow domain architects to provide consultancy, leadership and clear communication, and to champion software engineering and architectural best practice across teams. Drive AI and data innovation: guide the responsible application of generative AI, large language models, machine learning and knowledge-graph technologies to chemistry data, search and discovery use cases. Provide design and architecture governance: review changes, development projects and technical evaluations, ensuring solutions are scalable, secure, maintainable and cost-effective. Monitor domain health: track the design and operational health of the Chemistry Domain and write proposals to address risks, technical debt and emerging needs. Research and assess industry and technology advancements to identify opportunities to advance our technical capabilities and create new solutions in the chemistry space. Embed security and compliance: develop robust information-security and data-governance practices so we respond quickly and effectively to enterprise security issues. Lead troubleshooting: lead cross-functional teams to identify, research and coordinate the resources needed to diagnose and resolve complex Chemistry Domain issues. Other duties as assigned. Requirements:- Significant experience in software, network or systems architecture, with a strong grasp of architectural design, patterns and governance. Good working knowledge of more than one programming language. Practical, current experience applying AI/ML technologies — generative AI and large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, natural language processing, information retrieval or data mining — ideally at scale. Solid working knowledge of several of: cloud-native and distributed architectures (AWS, Azure or GCP), microservices and APIs, large-scale data platforms and databases, knowledge graphs and linked data, semantic search, and high-performance or parallel processing. Familiarity with modern data and ML engineering practices such as CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, containerisation and MLOps. Strong written, verbal and presentation skills, including communicating complex technical content to technical and non-technical audiences alike. A track record of contribution to complex technology projects in a global, matrixed environment. A natural ability to engage, influence and build relationships with stakeholders, teams and vendors across the business. A background or genuine interest in chemistry, life sciences or scientific data is highly desirable.
